newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds erased Thursday's losses, closing higher with most gains registered at the opening but on little volume as clients remained on the sidelines.
Dealers said the market finished short of its highs, falling midway through the afternoon as German Bund futures broke down through the key 100.00 level.
They said market players squared their positions ahead of the weekend and the Federal Open Market Committee meeting in the United States next Tuesday.
The market has discounted a 25 to 50 basis point hike in U.S. interest rates, primed by official comments.
"The market's feeling uncomfortable," said one trader.

One broker noted interest in a range of issues across the guilder yield curve, including switching from 2001 bonds into 2002 paper and buying of the new February 2007 10-year benchmark and the January 2023 long bellweather bonds.
"There's only really been domestics in the market today. Generally that's an indication of dedicated guilder traders," she said.
Another trader said the tone of the market changed from the morning, when buying ruled supreme.
"In the afternoon, we saw people who didn't want to sell all day, starting to sell when the market came down," he said.
He considered the market to be slightly short because it was cautious about the FOMC meeting. But he added: "If there's a rate hike, there will not be much reaction to it."

A Reuters poll of Dutch economists showed they expected Dutch bond yields to be barely changed in one month's time, perhaps a little lower than current levels. The yield curve and spread to Bunds were also forecast to change little.
One dealer said this meant nobody was too sure about the immediate outlook for interest rates.
